events.did: stepped into a dive bar as a brunette with a cropped cut and a boyish build
events.quote_anchor: She was a brunette now, slender with a boyish build. Short hair, straight back, small tits.

events.did: scanned the bar and found Rios sitting at the high-top in the far corner, her back to the wall
events.quote_anchor: scanned the room, until she found who she was looking for—the woman sitting at the high-top in the far corner

events.did: told Rios she was on leave until next week and had been thinking of getting out
events.quote_anchor: “Till next week,” said June. “But truth be told,” she added, picking at the label on her bottle, “I’ve been thinking of getting out.”

events.did: pinned Rios’s gun to the table before the ex-soldier could fire
events.quote_anchor: By the time Rios drew her gun, June had it pinned to the table, beers rattling from the force.

events.did: lifted her hand off Rios’s gun and told Rios not to harm the person she was wearing
events.quote_anchor: Then, slowly, she lifted her hand from the gun. Rios slid it off the table.

events.did: asked Rios how she squares working at EON
events.quote_anchor: “You do know what the E in EON stands for, right? So I guess I want to know, how do you square it?”

events.did: claimed she can become anyone she has met or touched, so long as they are still alive, and changed faces twice while saying it
events.quote_anchor: “Anyone I’ve met, so long as they’re still alive.” She sat forward, and as she did, she traded the neighbor for a blandly handsome white guy.

events.did: set a queen of spades with her number scrawled over the crown on the table and left the bar
events.quote_anchor: She set a playing card on the table, a queen of spades, her number scrawled over the crown.

relations.did: greeted June as Leigh, the friend whose body June was wearing, and put an arm around her shoulders
relations.quote_anchor: The woman looked up, her stern features cracking into a grin. “Leigh,” she said, rising to throw an arm around June’s borrowed shoulders.

relations.did: compared her work at Biohub Advance with her soldier days: fewer roadside bombs but plenty of headaches
relations.quote_anchor: Rios shrugged. “Less roadside bombs. Still plenty of headaches.”

relations.did: said EON keeps the world safe from people like June
relations.quote_anchor: “Because it keeps the world safe from people like you.”

relations.did: wore the body of Hugh, a middle-aged Black man and Rios’s upstairs neighbor, in front of Rios
relations.quote_anchor: June shrugged. “Fair.” She rolled her head on her neck, and as she did, she traded Leigh for Rios’s upstairs neighbor, Hugh, a middle-aged Black guy with graying hair.

numbers.did: entered the bar an hour after the hotel job
numbers.quote_anchor: THE woman who stepped into the bar an hour later was no longer blond.

numbers.did: said it had been closer to two years since she saw Rios
numbers.quote_anchor: “Closer to two,” June answered, grateful that Leigh kept tabs on things like that.

numbers.did: had four separate games playing on mute
numbers.quote_anchor: From the sticky floors to the trinkets plastering the walls to the four separate games playing on mute, the place was crowded, and raucous, and right up June’s alley.

numbers.did: claimed she had more than nine lives
numbers.quote_anchor: “Yes, well, lucky for me, I’ve got more than nine lives.

numbers.did: said there were a million better places than EON to work
numbers.quote_anchor: Rios hesitated. Shook her head. “There are a million better places.”
